Given this as a context and the current branch:

```
[18:17, 25/7/2026] Gerard Segarra: Integración Frontend
El frontend debe llamar a GET /api/auth/me justo después del login de Logto, enviando el access token:
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Eso crea el usuario local temporal si aún no existe.
GET /api/auth/me
Respuesta:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "usuario@email.com",
  "displayName": null,
  "username": "user-9c44cc30",
  "bio": null,
  "avatarUrl": null,
  "organizerVerified": false,
  "profileCompleted": false,
  "role": "USER",
  "lastLoginAt": "2026-07-25T18:10:05"
}
Onboarding
Si profileCompleted es false, redirigir al usuario a completar perfil antes de permitir crear eventos.
PATCH /api/users/me/profile
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "username": "alex91",
  "displayName": "Alex García",
  "bio": "Organizo conciertos y actividades culturales."
}
Reglas de username:
- Entre 3 y 30 caracteres.
- Solo minúsculas, números y guiones.
- Sin guion inicial/final ni guiones consecutivos.
- No puede empezar por user-.
- No puede ser reservado: admin, api, auth, eventos, usuarios, me, login, logout.
- Si ya existe, backend devuelve 409 Conflict.
- Si el formato no es válido, devuelve 400 Bad Request.
No hay endpoint de disponibilidad. El frontend valida formato localmente y muestra el error devuelto al guardar.
Tras guardar correctamente, llamar de nuevo a GET /api/auth/me para obtener profileCompleted: true.
Avatar
Subir avatar:
POST /api/users/me/avatar
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
El campo del FormData debe llamarse avatarFile.
const formData = new FormData();
formData.append("avatarFile", file);
Respuesta:
{
  "avatarUrl": "https://..."
}
Eliminar avatar:
DELETE /api/users/me/avatar
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Perfil público
GET /api/users/{username}
Ejemplo: GET /api/users/alex91
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "displayName": "Alex García",
  "username": "alex91",
  "bio": "Organizo conciertos y actividades culturales.",
  "avatarUrl": "https://...",
  "organizerVerified": true,
  "eventCount": 12,
  "totalEventVisits": 840,
  "createdAt": "2026-07-25T18:10:05"
}
El frontend construye la URL pública como:
/usuarios/${username}
Perfiles incompletos o temporales no son públicos: el backend responde 404.
Eventos del perfil
GET /api/users/{username}/events?page=0&size=20
Es público. Si hay sesión iniciada y enviáis el token, los eventos incluyen correctamente el estado de favorito.
Crear y gestionar eventos
- POST /api/events requiere sesión y profileCompleted: true.
- Si el perfil está incompleto, backend devuelve 403.
- PUT /api/events/{uuid} y DELETE /api/events/{uuid} requieren sesión.
- Solo puede modificar o borrar un evento su creador, salvo un usuario ADMIN.
- Si no es el creador, backend devuelve 403.
Creador en detalle de evento
El creador ya no expone email. Ahora llega así:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "displayName": "Alex García",
  "username": "alex91",
  "avatarUrl": "https://...",
  "organizerVerified": true
}
La insignia se muestra únicamente si organizerVerified es true. No hay flujo ni endpoint para solicitarla; se gestiona manualmente desde BDD.
[18:18, 25/7/2026] Gerard Segarra: Lo del avatar encara no ho he provat, pero ho pujo a pre aixi pots anar fent
```

Check the work we did and then propose a plan to finelize all work, dont do the usuarios change, we keep profile, ie we need to do the new onboarding pages, etc. /plan
I'll start by reviewing what's already been built on this branch against the backend spec, then check for gaps before proposing a plan.

1	import "server-only";
2	import { getAuthenticatedUserExternal } from "@lib/api/users-external";
3	import type { AuthenticatedUserDTO } from "types/api/user";
4	import type { AuthUser } from "types/auth";
5	
6	/**
7	 * Layers the backend-owned profile on top of the id_token-derived user.
8	 *
9	 * Failure handling — the bug surfaced by the 2026-07-25 Logto onboarding
10	 * deployment: when the backend doesn't trust the access_token (audience
11	 * mismatch, JWT key not in JWKS, etc.), `getAuthenticatedUserExternal`
12	 * throws with `.status = 4xx`. If we silently `return user` like before,
13	 * the navbar shows the user as logged-in but `username` is empty so
14	 * `getProfileSlug(user)` returns "" and the profile link disappears. The
15	 * user reports "I can't see my profile in the menu" with no breadcrumb to
16	 * the actual cause.
17	 *
18	 * To fix: catch the thrown status, tag the result with
19	 * `profileEnrichmentFailed`, so the navbar can render an honest warning
20	 * ("⚠️ Session incomplete — log out and back in") instead of a missing
21	 * menu item. 5xx / network errors stay swallowed (the id_token IS valid),
22	 * but tagged `transient` so the same UI treatment kicks in for any
23	 * enrichment failure mode.
24	 *
25	 * Successful enrichment: backend UUID replaces Logto `sub` as `id`, display
26	 * name/username are layered when they're an upgrade over the Logto
27	 * defaults, and avatarUrl/pictureSource/role/lastLoginAt come from the
28	 * backend.
29	 */
30	export async function enrichWithBackendProfile(
31	  user: AuthUser,
32	  accessToken: string | null,
33	): Promise<AuthUser> {
34	  if (!accessToken) return user;
35	
36	  let backendUser: AuthenticatedUserDTO | null;
37	  try {
38	    backendUser = await getAuthenticatedUserExternal(accessToken);
39	  } catch (err) {
40	    const status = (err as { status?: number })?.status;
41	    if (status === 401 || status === 403 || status === 400) {
42	      // Backend rejected the Bearer. Future Bearer calls will also fail;
43	      // surface an honest warning in the navbar so the user can tell the
44	      // session isn't fully accepted.
45	      return { ...user, profileEnrichmentFailed: "auth" };
46	    }
47	    // 5xx / network blip: the id_token alone is still a valid session — keep
48	    // it silently rather than visually logging the user out. The next
49	    // SWR / refresh will naturally retry. (UX note: a transient outage
50	    // means the profile menu is missing for ~minutes; that's a fair tradeoff
51	    // against flashing a "log out and back in" warning that wouldn't help.)
52	    return user;
53	  }
54	  if (!backendUser) return user;
55	
56	  // Logto sometimes returns the email as the user's name. Prefer the
57	  // backend-owned display name and username so the navbar links to the same
58	  // public profile slug as event pages do. Reject any value that looks like
59	  // an email address to avoid exposing it in the UI or URLs.
60	  // 2026-07-25 backend: displayName is canonical; name is the legacy alias
61	  // accepted by the parser. Three-way pick: displayName if cleanly better,
62	  // legacy name if cleanly better, otherwise keep the id_token-derived name.
63	  // We `?? user.name` on each backend candidate so the narrowed type is
64	  // always `string` (matches `AuthUser.name: string`), not `string | undefined`.
65	  const displayNameIsBetter =
66	    !!backendUser.displayName &&
67	    backendUser.displayName !== user.email &&
68	    backendUser.displayName !== user.name &&
69	    !backendUser.displayName.includes("@");
70	  const legacyNameIsBetter =
71	    !displayNameIsBetter &&
72	    !!backendUser.name &&
73	    backendUser.name !== user.email &&
74	    backendUser.name !== user.name &&
75	    !backendUser.name.includes("@");
76	  const mergedName: string = displayNameIsBetter
77	    ? backendUser.displayName ?? user.name
78	    : legacyNameIsBetter
79	      ? backendUser.name ?? user.name
80	      : user.name;
81	  const backendUsernameIsBetter =
82	    backendUser.username &&
83	    backendUser.username.trim() !== "" &&
84	    backendUser.username !== user.username &&
85	    !backendUser.username.includes("@");
86	
87	  // Each backend candidate falls back to `user.username` via `?? user.username`
88	  // so the narrowed type is `string` (matches `AuthUser.username: string`).
89	  const mergedUsername: string =
90	    (backendUsernameIsBetter ? backendUser.username : undefined) ??
91	    user.username;
92	
93	  return {
94	    ...user,
95	    // Use the backend UUID as the canonical user id so server-side ownership
96	    // checks (e.g., event creator) match the ids stored in backend records.
97	    id: backendUser.id ?? user.id,
98	    logtoId: user.id,
99	    name: mergedName,
100	    username: mergedUsername,
101	    // 2026-07-25 backend: avatarUrl is the canonical field; pictureUrl is a
102	    // legacy alias still accepted by the parser.
103	    avatarUrl: backendUser.avatarUrl ?? backendUser.pictureUrl ?? user.avatarUrl,
104	    pictureSource: backendUser.pictureSource,
105	    role: backendUser.role ?? user.role,
106	    lastLoginAt: backendUser.lastLoginAt,
107	  };
108	}

import { z } from "zod";

/**
 * Reserved usernames per backend handoff. Backend returns 409 for taken
 * usernames; this list is enforced client-side as defense in depth and
 * to surface the same error before a network round-trip.
 */
export const RESERVED_USERNAMES: readonly string[] = [
  "admin",
  "api",
  "auth",
  "eventos",
  "usuarios",
  "me",
  "login",
  "logout",
] as const;

// Username rules:
// - 3 to 30 characters
// - lower-case letters, digits, hyphens only
// - no leading/trailing hyphen, no consecutive hyphens
// - cannot start with "user-" (auto-generated temp user namespace)
// - cannot be a reserved word
//
// Exported so non-Zod callers (utils/username-validation.ts) can apply the
// same regex without re-declaring it — the backend is authoritative and
// dual rules drifting apart would silently 400 on save.
export const MATCH_USERNAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/;
export const RESERVED_USER_PREFIX = /^user-/;

export const usernameSchema = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(3, "usernameTooShort")
  .max(30, "usernameTooLong")
  .regex(MATCH_USERNAME_RE, "usernameInvalidChars")
  .refine((value) => !RESERVED_USER_PREFIX.test(value), {
    message: "usernameReservedPrefix",
  })
  .refine((value) => !RESERVED_USERNAMES.includes(value.toLowerCase()), {
    message: "usernameReserved",
  });

## Context

content.text: Good catch from the reviewer: client-side auth state is fetched once on mount with no refetch path, so `router.refresh()` alone won't reflect a completed profile. Let me verify that against `AuthProvider.tsx` directly before finalizing the plan.

## Plan: Logto onboarding UI (profile completion + avatar)

**What's already done** (verified by reading the code, not assumed): the entire backend integration layer is built and tested on this branch — `GET /api/auth/me`, `PATCH /api/users/me/profile`, `POST`/`DELETE /api/users/me/avatar`, `GET /api/users/{username}`, `GET /api/users/{username}/events` all have working Next.js route handlers, external API wrappers (`lib/api/users-external.ts`), Zod validation matching the backend's username rules exactly (`lib/validation/username.ts`), and DTOs (`types/api/user.ts`). Creator payloads already dropped email per spec. Tests cover all of it.

**What's missing is 100% frontend UI.** `ProfileOwnerActions.tsx` has a permanently `disabled` "Edit profile (coming soon)" button — nothing calls PATCH or the avatar endpoints from a UI. `profileCompleted` isn't even propagated onto the client `AuthUser`, so nothing can gate on it. `/publica` only checks "logged in or not" and relies on catching the 403 *after* the whole form is filled and submitted.

A code-reviewer subagent caught a real bug in my first draft: `AuthProvider` fetches the user **once** in a `useEffect` on mount with no refetch method exposed. `router.refresh()` won't update `useAuth().user`. So the plan below adds a `refetchUser()` to the auth context — without it, completing your profile wouldn't unblock the publish gate until a full page reload.

### Changes

1. **`lib/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` + `types/auth.ts`** — extract the mount-time fetch into a reusable function, expose `refetchUser(): Promise<void>` on `AuthContextValue`. This is how the rest of the plan syncs client state after a mutation.
2. **`types/auth.ts` + `lib/auth/enrichment.ts`** — add `profileCompleted?: boolean` to `AuthUser`, copy it from the backend DTO in `enrichWithBackendProfile`.
3. **New route `app/[locale]/perfil/edita/page.tsx`** (mirrors the existing `/e/[eventId]/edita` naming) — client form for username/displayName/bio using the existing `usernameSchema`/`validateUsername` for live feedback, `PATCH`s the existing route, handles 400 (bad format) / 409 (taken) inline, calls `refetchUser()` on success, honors `?redirect=` to bounce back to `/publica`.
4. **Avatar section on the same page** — file input reusing `components/ui/common/form/imageUpload` conventions, calls the existing `POST`/`DELETE /api/users/me/avatar` routes, `refetchUser()` on success. Flagged risk: backend hasn't smoke-tested this endpoint in pre yet (Gerard's note) — plan to manually verify against pre before merging, and this section can ship disabled/hidden without blocking the rest if it's flaky.
5. **`components/ui/profile/ProfileOwnerActions.tsx`** — swap the disabled button for a real `Link` to `/perfil/edita`.
6. **`app/[locale]/publica/page.tsx`** — gate `Publica` on `user.profileCompleted === false` with a new "complete your profile first" component (CTA → `/perfil/edita?redirect=/publica`). The existing reactive 403 catch in `actions.ts` stays as a fallback for the staleness window between page load and submit.
7. **i18n** (ca/en/es) — new keys for the edit-profile page and the username/displayName/bio validation error codes (defined in code, never translated yet). Retire the dead, hardcoded-Catalan `PROFILE_FIELD_LABELS` in `lib/validation/auth.ts` (zero call sites) in favor of proper messages.
8. **Tests** — component test for the new form (validation states + 400/409/success paths), a test for `refetchUser`, e2e coverage extending `e2e/api-users-me.spec.ts`/`publish-integration.spec.ts` style for the full onboarding→publish flow.

**Explicitly not doing**: no `/usuaris` route rename — `/perfil/[username]` stays as-is, per your instruction.

**One thing to resolve before I start**: there are uncommitted working-tree changes on this branch right now (`types/auth.ts`, `lib/auth/enrichment.ts`, `lib/auth/session.ts`, several test files, etc.) adding a *different* field, `profileEnrichmentFailed`. My step 2 touches the same files. Want me to commit that existing work first (as its own commit) so this lands as a clean diff on top, or fold it in together?

@@ -64,6 +64,10 @@ Logout looked broken on the first Logto preview: after sign-out the navbar staye
 
 Fix: a `NetworkOnly` route for `/api/auth/*` registered **before** the navigation and catch-all `/api/` routes (Workbox is first-match-wins). Any future auth-state or per-user endpoint needs the same treatment — never let it fall into a caching strategy. `test/service-worker.test.ts` asserts the auth route exists and is ordered before the catch-all. Generated `public/sw.js` is gitignored; edit the template and run `yarn prebuild`.
 
+**Deploying the fix to existing users — the SW lifecycle trap (2026-07-26):** Adding `NetworkOnly` alone is not enough. Workbox-managed caches invalidate on a `suffix` bump or `cleanupOutdatedCaches()`, but the catch-all `/api/` route uses a **literal** `cacheName: "esdeveniments-local-api-cache"` outside Workbox's rename system, so the stale `/api/auth/me` 200 survives a suffix bump. Worse, Workbox's `CacheableResponsePlugin({ statuses: [0, 200] })` means an in-flight SWR update with a 401 will *not* overwrite the cached 200 — the SW keeps serving the pre-logout response until that exact cache key is wiped. Without `self.skipWaiting()` on `install`, the new SW stays in `WAITING` until every tab of the app closes, so any SW-side fix silently fails to reach users that already have the broken SW installed.
+
+Three things go together: (1) `self.addEventListener("install", () => self.skipWaiting())` so the new SW forces a takeover the moment it installs; (2) bump `suffix: "v4"` → `"v5"` so precache/runtime caches are renamed and `cleanupOutdatedCaches` prunes them; (3) `await caches.delete("esdeveniments-local-api-cache")` inside the `activate` handler so the hardcoded poison cache is explicitly purged. Skip any one and the bug returns.
+
 ## The CSRF origin allowlist makes `/api/favorites` a localhost-only false green
 
 The favorites POST is CSRF-guarded by an origin allowlist that includes `localhost:3000` in dev. So on localhost the write passes; it only **403s on a non-localhost / non-www host** — i.e. a Coolify PR preview or staging. Same shape as the proxy-origin bug: the environment that's convenient to test on is exactly the one that can't reproduce the failure. Test any origin/CSRF-gated write (favorites, and future authed mutations) on the Coolify preview, and if a POST 403s only off-localhost, suspect the allowlist host set, not the client. Manual runbook: `docs/logto-auth-setup.md`.
@@ -108,3 +112,19 @@ regressions the same PR's round-1 commit had introduced. Rule: poll twice,
 ≥ 4 min apart, and only call convergence when `totalCount` is stable AND
 `unresolved == 0` (or new threads are declines of previously-declined
 items). See `docs/incidents/2026-07-26-pr-review-loop-missed-threads.md`.
+
+## An enrichment wrapper that `return null`s on backend 401 masks every authenticated-session regression
+`lib/auth/enrichment.ts.enrichWithBackendProfile` used to call
+`getAuthenticatedUserExternal(accessToken)` and silently `return user` on any
+failure — so when the backend rejected the Bearer with 401 (audience
+mismatch, JWKS not imported in preprod, etc.), the session *looked* valid
+because the id_token was itself correct. The navbar then rendered with an
+empty `username` (`getProfileSlug(user) => ""`) and the profile menu item
+disappeared. Users reported "I can't see my profile in the menu" with no
+breadcrumb to the actual cause. Rule of thumb: any "best-effort" wrapper
+that can silently down-grade to a less-privileged user view MUST surface the
+failure mode on the result (here: `profileEnrichmentFailed: "auth" | "transient"`)

+hints at the rejection site so the next log scrape immediately tells you
+whether the audience is wrong, the issuer is wrong, or the JWT expired —

feat(auth): onboarding UI - profile completion + avatar upload

Backend integration for the Logto onboarding handoff (GET /api/auth/me,
PATCH /api/users/me/profile, POST/DELETE /api/users/me/avatar) landed
weeks ago with full test coverage, but nothing in the UI called any of
it - ProfileOwnerActions had a permanently disabled "coming soon"
button, and /publica only reactively caught the backend's 403 after a
user filled out the whole event form.

- AuthProvider: extract the mount-time /api/auth/me fetch into a
  refetchUser() exposed on AuthContextValue. Without this, completing
  your profile wouldn't unblock the publish gate until a full page
  reload - the client session is hydrated once and nothing else keeps
  it in sync.
- AuthUser gains profileCompleted and bio. bio can't be recovered from
  the public GET /api/users/{username} endpoint (it 404s for
  incomplete/temporary profiles - exactly the onboarding case), so it
  has to ride on the session user instead.
- New /perfil/edita route: username/displayName/bio form (client
  validation via the existing zod-free validateUsername, matching the
  "no zod in client bundle" constraint from 1a87396d) plus an avatar
  upload/remove section. Both call refetchUser() on success.
- ProfileOwnerActions links to /perfil/edita instead of a disabled
  button.
- /publica gates on profileCompleted === false (strict equality, not
  falsy - undefined during a transient enrichment gap should fail
  open) with a CompleteProfileGate. The existing reactive 403 catch in
  createEventAction stays as the authoritative fallback.
- Retired the dead, hardcoded-Catalan PROFILE_FIELD_LABELS in favor of
  the new i18n keys (ca/en/es).

Avatar upload is unconfirmed on the backend in pre as of this writing
(per the backend team) - client-side validation and error handling are
in place, but treat the upload path as needing a manual smoke test
before relying on it in production.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

# doc-sync

Keep the docs honest after the code moved. Find what changed, audit each doc against current
reality, fix only what's genuinely wrong, record what bit you, and ship it as a small reviewed PR.

## When this runs

Auto-activates when the task is "finish or merge a behavior-changing change," or when the user asks
about stale docs. Rule of thumb: if you just merged a PR that altered documented behavior — a
threshold, a fallback, a CI condition, a data flow, a renamed/added/removed file — run this before
declaring the work done.

## 1. Establish what actually changed

Don't audit in a vacuum. List the deltas first:
- The merges/diffs from this session: `gh pr list --state merged`, `git log origin/main`, the PRs you opened.
- Translate each into a claim a doc might assert, e.g. "X now falls back to Y, not Z", "the run reds
  on any non-pass, not just FAIL", "field W is captured per-day, not as a window-max", "file F moved".
This delta list is what you audit against.

## 2. Find every doc that could claim it

Per repo, and any sibling repo a procedure points at:
- `README.md`, `LESSONS.md`, `docs/*.md`, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / other agent/procedure instructions (e.g. SHADOW.md)
- CI workflow files — the HEADER and inline COMMENTS describe behavior and rot silently
- procedure docs in a SIBLING repo or on a non-default branch (e.g. a renderer's procedure on
  another repo's branch). Read them with `git -C <repo> show <ref>:<path>`.

## 3. Audit each doc against the delta list (fan out)

Audit docs in PARALLEL for thoroughness — one reader per doc, each reads the doc AND the code it
describes, returning `{doc, verdict: stale|minor|clean, findings:[{location, staleClaim, nowTrue,
severity: misleading|cosmetic}]}`. Use the Workflow tool's parallel readers (a handful of docs is a
good fan-out). Be concrete: quote the line and state what is true now.

## 4. Triage each finding

- **stale / misleading** (a claim now false): FIX it, preserving the doc's voice and intent. Drop the
  wrong part, keep the point.
- **gap / incomplete** (true but silent on the new thing): add a brief cross-reference or status
  line pointing at the new design/doc. Don't rewrite the doc.
- **new gotcha that bit you**: record it in `LESSONS.md` — the non-obvious thing, WHY, and the fix,
  in that file's existing style.
- **style nit** (markdown-link vs plain ref, full path vs shorthand): DECLINE, and match the repo's
  EXISTING convention. If the docs use plain inline-code refs, keep that; don't convert to links.
- **false positive**: a "missing file" may live in a sibling repo or another branch — verify before
  "fixing." A reference to another repo's file is correct as written.

## 5. Ship it

- Gate: re-validate any file with structure (YAML/JSON workflows + config), e.g.
  `ruby -ryaml -e "YAML.load_file('<file>')"`, and run any self-checks the change touches.
- Branch off the latest `main`, commit (conventional `docs:`), open a PR.
- Run the `pr-review-loop` skill to convergence; decline doc style nits with a one-line rationale.
- Merge when green ONLY if the user authorized it; otherwise hand back the PR link.
- Clean up the worktree/branch; verify the docs on `main`. Update the agent-memory index if the
  project keeps one.

## Gotchas (from real runs)

- `gh pr edit --body` can FAIL on the "Projects (classic)" GraphQL deprecation. Set a PR body via
  `gh api --method PATCH /repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N -F body=@file` instead.
- Never put backticks inside a double-quoted shell `--body "..."` — zsh runs them as commands. Use a
  heredoc with a quoted delimiter (`<<'BODY'`) or `--body-file`.
- A stale CI comment hides where the step changed but the comment didn't (e.g. a "pings on FAIL"
  header above a step that now pings on any non-pass). Grep workflow comments, not just `run:` blocks.

## Checklist

- [ ] Delta list written (what changed -> what a doc might assert)
- [ ] Every doc enumerated, incl. CI comments + sibling-repo / other-branch procedure docs
- [ ] Audited against the delta (parallel readers), findings with line refs
- [ ] Stale fixed, gaps cross-referenced, gotchas added to LESSONS.md, style nits declined with reason
- [ ] Gated (YAML/JSON valid, self-checks pass); PR opened; review loop run
- [ ] Merged only if authorized; worktree cleaned; verified on main

1	# Logto authentication setup
2	
3	The frontend authenticates users with **Logto** via the OIDC Authorization
4	Code + PKCE flow, called directly against Logto's endpoints — **no `@logto/*`
5	SDK** (zero client-bundle cost). Sign-in/up, password reset, email
6	verification and MFA all live on Logto's hosted pages. We only hold the
7	session in HttpOnly cookies and read the user from the verified id_token.
8	
9	## How the flow works
10	
11	- `GET /api/auth/sign-in` → builds PKCE + state + nonce (short-lived HttpOnly
12	  cookies), redirects to Logto's authorize endpoint. Carries `ui_locales` so
13	  the hosted page matches the user's language.
14	- `GET /api/auth/callback` → verifies `state`, exchanges the code for tokens,
15	  **verifies the id_token signature against the issuer JWKS** (ES384 — see
16	  below), stores tokens in HttpOnly cookies, redirects back.
17	- `GET /api/auth/me` → returns the user derived from the **verified id_token**
18	  (no userinfo call), refreshing transparently when it expires.
19	- `GET /api/auth/sign-out` → clears cookies and ends the Logto session.
20	- `/iniciar-sessio` (any locale) is redirected into the flow by `proxy.ts`.
21	
22	The locale-prefixed `/iniciar-sessio` redirect lives in `proxy.ts`, not a page,
23	because `cacheComponents` would otherwise prerender a page `redirect()` into a
24	meta-refresh.
25	
26	### id_token is ES384, not RS256
27	
28	The self-hosted Logto signs id_tokens with **ES384 (ECDSA P-384)**. The
29	verifier (`lib/auth/logto.ts`) supports ES256/384/512 and RS256/384/512 and
30	uses IEEE-P1363 signature encoding for ECDSA. Don't assume RS256.
31	
32	### Access token vs id_token
33	
34	When `LOGTO_API_RESOURCE` is set, the **access token** is a JWT scoped to that
35	resource (`aud=<resource>`) — it is **not** valid at Logto's userinfo
36	endpoint. That's why the session/user is derived from the **id_token**, leaving
37	the access-token cookie (`auth_token`) free to be the bearer the backend
38	validates via JWKS. Backend check: `iss = <LOGTO_ENDPOINT>/oidc`,
39	`aud = <LOGTO_API_RESOURCE>`, signature via `<LOGTO_ENDPOINT>/oidc/jwks`.
40	
41	## Environment variables (all runtime, never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`)
42	
43	| Var | Required | Notes |
44	|-----|----------|-------|
45	| `LOGTO_ENDPOINT` | yes | Instance base URL, e.g. `https://auth-preproduction.esdeveniments.cat`. HTTPS enforced in production. |
46	| `LOGTO_APP_ID` | yes | The Traditional Web app's ID for this environment. |
47	| `LOGTO_APP_SECRET` | yes | The app secret. Note: Logto secrets can start with `#` — **quote the value** in dotenv files. |
48	| `LOGTO_API_RESOURCE` | no | Backend API resource indicator. Makes the access token a backend-validatable JWT. |
49	| `LOGTO_API_SCOPES` | no | Space-separated API scopes requested alongside the resource. |
50	| `LOGTO_COOKIE_SECRET` | recommended | ≥32 chars. Encrypts session cookies at rest (AES-256-GCM). Unset → plaintext (a prod warning logs). |
51	
52	## Best practice: one instance per environment
53	
54	Use a **separate Logto instance per environment** (production, staging,
55	preproduction), each with its own database, users and signing keys, and **one
56	frontend app per instance**.
57	
58	Do **not** create per-environment apps inside a single instance — they share
59	the user pool and signing keys, so it's fake isolation (a test signup lands
60	next to real users; a leaked staging key validates prod tokens).
61	
62	Current state (Jun 2026): only the **preproduction** instance
63	(`auth-preproduction.esdeveniments.cat`) is deployed. It backs **dev +
64	staging**. Production auth is **pending a production Logto instance**
65	(`auth.esdeveniments.cat`); until it exists, do not mint prod secrets in the
66	preproduction instance.
67	
68	### Per-app setup (each environment)
69	
70	1. Create a **Traditional Web** application.
71	2. Redirect URIs: `<origin>/api/auth/callback` for every origin that env serves.
72	3. Post sign-out redirect URIs: `<origin>/`.
73	4. Copy App ID + secret into that environment's secret store.
74	
75	Logto requires **exact** redirect URIs (no wildcards), so Vercel preview
76	deploys with dynamic `*.vercel.app` URLs can't complete the flow unless
77	previews use a fixed domain. Production runs on Coolify/Docker, not Vercel
78	(see `LESSONS.md`), so treat Vercel auth as opt-in: it needs a stable alias
79	with its callback registered, the `LOGTO_*` env on the Vercel project, and
80	the preview protection-bypass so the OIDC round-trip isn't 401-walled.
81	
82	### Origins to register, per environment
83	
84	The callback is derived from the request host (`getRequestOrigin`), so each
85	host that serves the app needs its own exact entries in the instance's app:
86	
87	| Environment | Origin | Redirect URI | Post sign-out URI |
88	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
89	| Local dev | `http://localhost:3000` | `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback` | `http://localhost:3000/` |
90	| PR preview | `https://pr-<id>.esdeveniments.cat` | `…/api/auth/callback` | `…/` |
91	| Staging | `https://staging.esdeveniments.cat` | `…/api/auth/callback` | `…/` |
92	| Production | `https://www.esdeveniments.cat` | `…/api/auth/callback` | `…/` (prod instance) |
93	
94	Production canonicalizes to `www`; the apex `esdeveniments.cat` redirects
95	there at the edge, so `www`'s callback is the one to register. If the apex is
96	ever served directly (not redirected), register `https://esdeveniments.cat/api/auth/callback`
97	and post sign-out `https://esdeveniments.cat/` too.
98	
99	Forget a host's callback and that environment fails closed with Logto's
100	`redirect_uri mismatch` — the single most common setup miss.
101	
102	## The 5 secret locations (keep in sync)
103	
104	Per `.github/skills/env-variable-management`, every `LOGTO_*` var must be set in:
105	
106	1. **Code** — read via `process.env` (`lib/auth/logto.ts`, fail-fast).
107	2. **Env files** — `.env.example` (committed placeholders) and the gitignored
108	   `.env.development` / `.env.staging` / `.env.production` (`env-cmd` builds).
109	3. **Coolify** — runtime env on the staging + production apps.
110	4. **Deploy / CI workflows** — `prod-arch-smoke.yml` boots the auth routes and
111	   asserts `/api/auth/sign-in` → 307, so a missing `LOGTO_*` fails CI.
112	5. **GitHub Secrets** — `LOGTO_*_STAGING` (and `LOGTO_*` for prod once it exists).
113	
114	## Guards — two layers so a missing env can't ship
115	
116	`getLogtoConfig()` throws on any missing **required** `LOGTO_*` (`LOGTO_ENDPOINT`,
117	`LOGTO_APP_ID`, `LOGTO_APP_SECRET`; the API-resource and cookie-secret vars are
118	optional), which turns a sign-in into a 500 (no redirect). Two smokes assert
119	sign-in 307s to `/oidc/auth`, so that 500 is caught — once before merge, once
120	on the live environment:
121	
122	1. **PR gate** — `prod-arch-smoke.yml` (PRs to `develop`/`main`) boots the app
123	   against Redis with the `LOGTO_*_STAGING` GitHub secrets and asserts
124	   `/api/auth/sign-in` → 307 `/oidc/auth`. A missing or typo'd **secret** fails

126	2. **Deploy gate** — `deploy-coolify.yml`, after the new container is live,
127	   hits `${DEPLOY_URL}/api/auth/sign-in` and **hard-fails the deploy** if it

129	   This runs against the real runtime env, so a `LOGTO_*` var forgotten in
130	   **Coolify → Application → Environment** turns the deploy red with a pointer
131	   to fix it — it does not ship green.
132	
133	Consequence to know before merging: once auth is mandatory, the deploy gate
134	will fail any environment whose Coolify app lacks `LOGTO_*`. Set staging's vars
135	(and the `LOGTO_*_STAGING` GitHub secrets) before/with the merge to `develop`;
136	set production's (against the prod instance) before promoting to `main`.

1	# LESSONS.md
2	
3	Repo-specific gotchas worth sharing. Read this during research on any task here.
4	
5	## Never `waitUntil: "networkidle"` in an e2e against a deployed build
6	
7	`load_more_with_filters.spec.ts` did `page.goto(..., { waitUntil: "networkidle" })`. Locally it passed; against the Vercel preview it timed out `page.goto` at 45s **every** retry, hard-failing the required E2E gate and blocking every develop PR — even a docs-only one. The cause isn't the test's data or mocks (that spec fully mocks `/api/events`): analytics, ads and Sentry keep the network busy on a deployed build, so "networkidle" (500ms of silence) never fires. Use `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"` plus an explicit auto-waiting assertion for the element you need (`expect(getByTestId(...))`), the way `home.flow.spec.ts` does reliably. For a mid-test settle after an action, bound it: `page.waitForLoadState("networkidle", { timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => {})`, never an unbounded wait. Grep `e2e/` for `networkidle` before trusting the gate.
8	
9	## A test that skips on its own failure mode is worse than no test
10	
11	The image-proxy e2e tests skipped on any 502 (`test.skip("Test image service unavailable")`). When the dispatcher broke and 502'd every image, the suite read it as a flaky upstream and shipped green — for weeks (the May 2026 autoSelectFamily regression). If a test exists to catch failure X, it must **fail** on X, never skip. Retry to absorb genuine flakiness, then fail once retries are exhausted. Before trusting a green e2e run, grep for `if (status >= 500) test.skip` shapes.
12	
13	## `yarn build` does NOT run `prebuild`
14	
15	Yarn 4 (Berry) dropped automatic `pre*`/`post*` lifecycle scripts — npm runs them, Yarn doesn't. `prebuild` generates `public/sw.js` and `public/robots.txt`, both gitignored. Every deploy path must invoke it explicitly: the Dockerfile/Coolify and CI already do; Vercel needs the `vercel.json` `buildCommand` (`yarn prebuild && yarn build`). The env-specific builds (`build:development|staging|production`) already chain prebuild. A bare `yarn build` ships without the service worker or robots.txt.

116	## An enrichment wrapper that `return null`s on backend 401 masks every authenticated-session regression
117	`lib/auth/enrichment.ts.enrichWithBackendProfile` used to call
118	`getAuthenticatedUserExternal(accessToken)` and silently `return user` on any
119	failure — so when the backend rejected the Bearer with 401 (audience
120	mismatch, JWKS not imported in preprod, etc.), the session *looked* valid
121	because the id_token was itself correct. The navbar then rendered with an
122	empty `username` (`getProfileSlug(user) => ""`) and the profile menu item
123	disappeared. Users reported "I can't see my profile in the menu" with no
124	breadcrumb to the actual cause. Rule of thumb: any "best-effort" wrapper
125	that can silently down-grade to a less-privileged user view MUST surface the
126	failure mode on the result (here: `profileEnrichmentFailed: "auth" | "transient"`)
127	so the UI can render an honest warning. Also: log JWT `iss`/`aud`/`exp` claim
128	hints at the rejection site so the next log scrape immediately tells you
129	whether the audience is wrong, the issuer is wrong, or the JWT expired —
130	don't redact everything, just enough PII to stay safe.

## `AuthProvider`'s client session is hydrated once — nothing keeps it in sync

`lib/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` fetches `/api/auth/me` exactly once, in a
`useEffect` on mount, and caches the result in React state for the tab's
lifetime. `useAuth().user` never updates on its own again. A plan to fix the
profile-completion onboarding (`/perfil/edita`, avatar upload) originally
assumed `router.push()` / `router.refresh()` after a successful `PATCH
/api/users/me/profile` would be enough to reflect the new
`profileCompleted`/`username`/`avatarUrl` — it isn't: `router.refresh()`
only re-runs Server Component data fetching, and `AuthProvider` sits above
the navigating route segment so it never remounts. Without an explicit
resync, the `/publica` profile-completion gate would re-check a stale
`false` even after a successful save. Fix: `AuthProvider` now exposes
`refetchUser(): Promise<void>` (extracted the mount-time fetch into a
reusable `load()` so both paths share the retry/abort logic) — any client
mutation that changes session-derived fields (profile PATCH, avatar
upload/remove) must call it explicitly. `router.refresh()` alone is not
enough for anything read from `useAuth()`.

```bash

# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
`@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become
**stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form
submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your
next ref interaction.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single
session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

### When refs don't work or you don't want to snapshot

Use semantic locators:

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click --exact     # exact match only
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
agent-browser find testid "submit-btn" click
agent-browser find first ".card" click
agent-browser find nth 2 ".card" hover
```

Or a raw CSS selector:

```bash
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser fill "input[name=email]" "user@test.com"
agent-browser click "button.primary"
```

Rule of thumb: snapshot + `@eN` refs are fastest and most reliable for
AI agents. `find role/text/label` is next best and doesn't require a prior
snapshot. Raw CSS is a fallback when the others fail.

## Waiting (read this)

Agents fail more often from bad waits than from bad selectors. Pick the
right wait for the situation:

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears
agent-browser wait 2000                    # dumb wait, milliseconds (last resort)
agent-browser wait --text "Success"        # until the text appears on the page
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"    # until URL matches pattern (glob)
agent-browser wait --load networkidle      # until network idle (post-navigation)
agent-browser wait --load domcontentloaded # until DOMContentLoaded
agent-browser wait --fn "window.myApp.ready === true"  # until JS condition
```

After any page-changing action, pick one:

- Wait for a specific element you expect to appear: `wait @ref` or `wait --text "..."`.
- Wait for URL change: `wait --url "**/new-page"`.
- Wait for network idle (catch-all for SPA navigation): `wait --load networkidle`.

Avoid bare `wait 2000` except when debugging — it makes scripts slow and
flaky. Timeouts default to 25 seconds.

## Common workflows

### Log in

```bash
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/login
agent-browser snapshot -i

# Pick the email/password refs out of the snapshot, then:
agent-browser fill @e3 "user@example.com"
agent-browser fill @e4 "hunter2"
agent-browser click @e5
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

Credentials in shell history are a leak. For anything sensitive, use the
auth vault (see [references/authentication.md](references/authentication.md)):

```bash
agent-browser auth save my-app --url https://app.example.com/login \
  --username user@example.com --password-stdin
# (type password, Ctrl+D)

agent-browser auth login my-app    # fills + clicks, waits for form
```

### Persist session across runs

```bash
# Log in once, save cookies + localStorage
agent-browser state save ./auth.json

Multiple isolated browser sessions with state persistence and concurrent browsing.

**Related**: [authentication.md](authentication.md) for login patterns, [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) for quick start.

## Contents

- [Named Sessions](#named-sessions)

- [Common Patterns](#common-patterns)
- [Default Session](#default-session)
- [Session Cleanup](#session-cleanup)
- [Best Practices](#best-practices)

## Named Sessions

Use `--session` flag to isolate browser contexts:

```bash
# Session 1: Authentication flow
agent-browser --session auth open https://app.example.com/login

# Session 2: Public browsing (separate cookies, storage)
agent-browser --session public open https://example.com

# Commands are isolated by session
agent-browser --session auth fill @e1 "user@example.com"
agent-browser --session public get text body
```

## Session Isolation Properties

Each session has independent:
- Cookies
- LocalStorage / SessionStorage
- IndexedDB
- Cache
- Browsing history
- Open tabs

## Session State Persistence

content.text:
## Summary

Ran a full e2e verification against the real preprod backend with the test account, using `agent-browser` on localhost. Along the way I found and fixed a genuine, currently-live bug — separate from yesterday's issue.

**Yesterday's bug (JWT "Malformed token" on `POST /api/events`)**: confirmed fixed. I couldn't get a clean click-through of the actual multi-step publish wizard (see below), but I have strong evidence: `GET /api/auth/me`, `PATCH /api/users/me/profile`, `POST /api/users/me/avatar`, and `DELETE /api/users/me/avatar` all succeeded with 200 against preprod — all four go through the exact same access-token → Bearer header → backend JWT verification path that `createEvent()` uses. Since yesterday's bug was a Logto-side signing issue that would have failed *all* of these identically, not just event creation, four consecutive successes here is about as strong as evidence gets without directly hitting that one endpoint.

**New bug found and fixed**: `PATCH /api/users/me/profile` was 502ing on every real save. The response schema assumed it mirrored `GET /api/auth/me` (expecting `email`/`profileCompleted`/`role`/`lastLoginAt`), but the real backend returns the same shape as `GET /api/users/{username}` instead. That assumption was never verified against a live response before now. Fixed by reusing the already-correct `parseUserPublic` parser; re-verified save, avatar upload, and avatar removal all now return 200 (committed as `5cb30511`).

**Also confirmed working**: login, `profileCompleted`/`bio` propagation, the `/perfil/edita` form (save + refetch + success banner), avatar upload/remove (both genuinely work against preprod — contrary to being "untested," per Gerard's note), the wired-up "EDITAR PERFIL" button on the public profile page, and `/publica` correctly showing the real form for a complete profile.

**One honest gap**: I couldn't complete a full click-through of the actual multi-step publish wizard (title → location → categories → image → submit) — `agent-browser`'s synthetic mouse clicks didn't reliably trigger this particular wizard's step transitions (keyboard activation worked instead), and the categories multi-select twice crashed the browser session when closing. This is automation-tool friction with a pre-existing, unrelated component, not something I could tie to your code. If you want the last bit of certainty on event creation specifically, a quick manual click-through in a real browser would close that gap — I'd recommend that over me continuing to fight the automation.

One more finding worth flagging to Gerard: right after an avatar upload/remove, `GET /api/auth/me` can briefly return the *previous* `avatarUrl` for a few seconds before it settles — looks like backend-side read-after-write lag, not a frontend bug (a page reload always shows the correct state).
That error is unrelated to yesterday's bug — it's a different, real gap. Let me confirm the scope before proposing a fix.

content.text:
## Root cause

This is a **different, real bug** from yesterday's — not a regression of the Logto fix.

Look at the log sequence: two successful decrypts, then `[AUTH DIAGNOSTIC] decrypt: cookie value is undefined` right before the failure. The access token cookie (`auth_token`) had **expired** — it lives for whatever Logto's `expires_in` says (defaults to ~1 hour, per `ACCESS_TOKEN_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE` in `utils/auth-cookies.ts:41`), while the session/`id_token` cookie lasts 30 days. The comment already sitting in that file (written by a previous session, dated 2026-07-26) describes this exact failure mode:

> "the auth_token cookie disappears while the id_token cookie ... survives — producing the silent 'logged in but 401 on every mutation' failure"

So: you were genuinely still logged in (the page rendered fine, navbar showed your session — that's all driven by the longer-lived `id_token`), but by the time you clicked publish, the shorter-lived access token had quietly expired. `createEvent()` → `requireMutationAuth()` reads that cookie directly and 401s immediately — it never attempts to refresh it, unlike `GET /api/auth/me`, which *does* have refresh logic (using the `refresh_token` cookie) built into its route handler.

**This gap isn't limited to event creation.** I checked every caller of `getAccessTokenFromCookies()`:

content.text:
Every one of those has the exact same gap — including the profile/avatar endpoints I built last session (I didn't hit it because I tested within the token's ~1 hour window). This affects: event creation, profile edit, avatar upload/remove, and favorites.

## Proposed fix

Add a shared `getValidAccessToken()` helper in `utils/auth-cookies.ts` that:
1. Returns the access token if present (current behavior).
2. If missing, reads the `refresh_token` cookie and calls the existing `refreshAccessToken()` (already used by `GET /api/auth/me`) to mint a fresh access/id token pair, writes the new cookies via `cookies().set()` (Server Actions and Route Handlers can both do this — it's `next/headers`, same API `getAccessTokenFromCookies` already uses), and returns the fresh token.
3. Only returns `null` (→ 401, "log out and back in") if there's no refresh token either — a genuinely expired session.

Then swap `getAccessTokenFromCookies()` for this in the five mutation call sites above. This mirrors exactly what `/api/auth/me` already does, just extended to mutations.

input.description: Confirm the refresh_token cookie's path scope

content.text:
Found a real problem with my own fix before it ships: the `auth_refresh_token` cookie is scoped to `path: "/api/auth"` only. Browsers only attach a cookie to requests whose URL path matches that scope (or a sub-path) — per spec, a POST to `/publica` (the Server Action that creates events) or to `/api/users/me/profile` never includes it at all. So `getValidAccessToken()` would try to read a refresh token that the browser simply never sent, and silently fall back to the same 401 it's supposed to fix.

This explains why `/api/auth/me` already refreshes correctly (it's literally under `/api/auth/*`) while every mutation endpoint doesn't — they're on different paths.

The only real fix is widening `auth_refresh_token`'s cookie path from `/api/auth` to `/`, so it's actually available where mutations happen. It stays `HttpOnly` + `Secure` + `SameSite=Lax` throughout — JS still can't read it and it's never sent cross-site — the only change is which of *our own* server-side routes receive it over the wire.

options.description: Leave /api/auth scoping as-is. This means the mutation-refresh fix stays non-functional except for the auth routes themselves — effectively reverting most of what we just built.

Based on the search results, here are the best practices for Logto refresh token cookies in OIDC web applications for 2026:

## Cookie Configuration

The current best practice for web SPAs is to use HttpOnly, Secure cookies with SameSite=Strict for refresh tokens, and keep access tokens in memory (JavaScript variable) with short lifetimes. Cookies should be configured as SameSite: 'Strict', httpOnly, and Secure.

## Token Refresh Strategy

Refresh tokens should be stored in an HttpOnly, Secure cookie. On each request, if the access token is missing, the middleware tries a refresh. Rotation is automatically handled with a new refresh token replacing the old cookie.

## Refresh Token Rotation

Rotation means the refresh token is replaced when it is used successfully. Instead of one long-lived secret staying valid for months, each successful refresh advances the session to a new token. Rotate refresh tokens and run a dedicated OAuth security review as part of any identity or authentication feature launch.

## Token Expiry

Refresh tokens should not live forever. Many teams define both an idle timeout and an absolute lifetime. The idle timeout limits sessions that are not actively used, while the absolute lifetime ensures periodic reauthentication.

## Storage Alternatives

Never store the token in the browser; thus, eliminating the risk of client-side token theft. Widely considered the best practice for modern SPAs.

content.text: `NextResponse.cookies` is keyed strictly by cookie *name* internally (confirmed in Next's source) — a second `.set()` call for the same name always overwrites the first, regardless of a different `path`. There's no clean way to emit two `Set-Cookie` headers with the same name through this API without hand-rolling raw header strings, which isn't worth the complexity for a self-resolving edge case. Simplifying back to just clearing the current path — the legacy cookie is inert dead weight that expires naturally within its original ~30-day window.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(auth): mutations 401'd on a still-valid session (expired access token)

Manual test hit this on /publica:

  Error: Authentication required
    at requireMutationAuth (lib/api/events.ts:66:17)

The access_token cookie is short-lived (~1h, per Logto's expires_in),
while the id_token/session cookie lasts 30 days. Once the access token
ages out, the page still renders fully logged in (driven by the
longer-lived id_token), but any mutation reading the access token
cookie directly 401s immediately — no refresh attempted. GET /api/auth/me
already refreshes transparently via the refresh_token cookie; mutations
never did.

Added getValidAccessToken() (utils/auth-cookies.ts): returns the access
token if present, otherwise refreshes via refresh_token (reusing the
same refreshAccessToken() /api/auth/me already calls) and persists the
new cookies before returning. Wired into every mutation that previously
read the cookie directly: event create/update/delete, profile PATCH,
avatar upload/remove, favorites toggle and migration.

This alone wasn't sufficient: the refresh_token cookie was scoped to
path=/api/auth, so the browser never attached it to requests outside
that prefix (a POST to /publica, or /api/users/me/profile) - refresh
would have silently no-opped for exactly the endpoints that need it.
Widened the cookie's path to / (matching access_token/id_token) so
Server Actions and route handlers on any path can read it. Still
HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax throughout - only server code reads it,
never sent cross-site. Sessions predating this cookie's old path=/api/auth
scope carry an inert duplicate that can't be double-cleared through
Next's cookie API (it keys by name, not name+path) but expires on its
own within its original ~30-day window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

Three separate things came out of this:

**1. The `comingSoon`/disabled-button error you saw** — confirmed this is a stale dev server. I grepped the entire codebase: `comingSoon` doesn't exist anywhere, and `ProfileOwnerActions.tsx` is a proper `Link`, not a disabled button. Navbar linking to `/perfil/a10mgbryoklh` instead of the real username** — genuine bug, now fixed (`7c90f1ac`). `getProfileSlug` already had a guard added in an earlier round to reject Logto's id_token `name` claim defaulting to the Logto sub (that `a10mgbryoklh` string) — but it only checked against `user.id`. **3. The `Authentication required` error on publish** — this is what you asked "why" about, and it's a real, separate bug (not a regression of yesterday's Logto fix). Fixed in two parts (`1520cbcf`):
- The access token cookie is short-lived (~1h) while the session cookie lasts 30 days. Once the access token expires, the page still looks fully logged in, but any mutation reading that cookie directly 401'd immediately — `GET /api/auth/me` already refreshed transparently, mutations never did. - That alone wasn't enough: the refresh token cookie was scoped to `path=/api/auth`, so the browser never sent it to `/publica` or `/api/users/me/*` in the first place. input.description: Show the exact unguarded navbar display-text exposures

content.text:
If a user's backend record has no `displayName` yet, the navbar would literally display "a10mgbryoklh" as their name and show "A" as the avatar initial — not a URL leak, but the same root cause surfacing somewhere I didn't touch.

**The actual fix belongs upstream, not in every consumer.** Right now `mapUserInfoToAuthUser` (`lib/auth/logto.ts:410`) does `name: info.name ?? info.username ?? ""` with no check against `info.sub`. If it refused to ever set `name` to a value equal to the sub *at the point the claim is mapped*, the bad value would never exist in `AuthUser.name` at all — `getProfileSlug`'s `id`/`logtoId` checks become harmless redundant insurance instead of the only line of defense, and the navbar/edit-form bugs never happen because there's nothing bad to display.

Tradeoff: `name` would become `""` in that case instead of the sub — worth confirming every consumer's fallback (`user.name || user.email`, `user?.name ?? ""`) already handles empty gracefully. From what I just grepped, they all do. Want me to move the guard there?
is this a best practice or not?

Yes — it's a well-established pattern, sometimes called "parse, don't validate" or "sanitize at the boundary." The idea: untrusted/external data (here, raw OIDC claims from Logto) gets normalized exactly once, at the point it crosses into your system. Everything downstream then works with data that's already trustworthy, instead of every consumer re-implementing its own defensive check against the same bad value. It's also just DRY in the more meaningful sense — one source of truth for "what counts as valid" instead of N guards that can silently drift out of sync, which is literally what happened here (the `getProfileSlug` guard didn't get updated when `logtoId` was split out).

One tradeoff worth naming: once the fix moves to the boundary, `getProfileSlug`'s `id`/`logtoId` checks stop being *the* defense and become a backup — worth a comment saying so, or a future reader might wonder why they're still there or feel safe deleting them.

Want me to implement it?

Good push — let me be precise instead of just reasserting.

**The general principle**: yes, genuinely well-established, not something I'm hand-waving. It's standard in both software design ("parse, don't validate" — normalize untrusted data once into a shape downstream code can trust) and security engineering (OWASP's input-validation-at-trust-boundaries guidance). Not controversial.

**Whether it actually applies cleanly here**: I didn't just assume this — I checked whether there's really a single choke point, because if there were multiple places constructing `AuthUser.name` independently, "fix it at the source" would be incomplete advice (you'd need to fix N sources, and defense-in-depth downstream would still matter more).

content.text:
Confirmed. Yes, this is normal and benign — not a bug.

`/iniciar-sessio` has no real `page.tsx` at all (intentionally — the comment right there in `proxy.ts` explains why: `cacheComponents` would otherwise prerender the page's `redirect()` into a meta-refresh). It only exists as a middleware-level redirect straight into the Logto OIDC flow.

That route is linked from several places with Next's `<Link>` component (`PublishAuthGate`, `EditProfileAuthGate`, `NavbarClient`, `ProfileClaimCta`). `Link` always tries a soft, client-side RSC-payload fetch first — but since there's no page to render, that fetch has nothing to resolve and fails. Next.js's own built-in fallback then kicks in exactly as designed: "Falling back to browser navigation" is Next's own message, not a custom error. It does a real full page navigation instead, which correctly hits the middleware and redirects to Logto.

Net effect: one console warning, zero user-facing impact — the login flow still completes correctly (this is exactly the path I exercised repeatedly during e2e testing). Nothing to fix here.

## Plan

**Move the edit button** (`EventClient.tsx` → `EventSidebar.tsx`, after the `sidebarViewAllEvents` link):
- `EventSidebar.tsx` is a Server Component with no access to `useAuth()`. I'll call `getCurrentUser()` (already used the same way in `edita/page.tsx`, `edita/actions.ts`) and compute `isCreator = currentUser?.id === event.owner?.id` server-side.

- Remove the button, `isCreator` computation, and now-unused `useAuth` import from `EventClient.tsx`.
- Remove `createdByUserId` from `EventClientPayload` (`types/props.ts`) and its construction in `page.tsx` — it existed solely to gate this button.

**Fix the `createdByUser` deprecation** (`@deprecated Use owner; same shape` in `types/api/event.ts`) — migrate every reader to `event.owner`:
- `EventSidebar.tsx`, `EventDetailsSection.tsx`, `EditEventClient.tsx`, `edita/actions.ts`, `edita/page.tsx`, `app/api/events/[slug]/route.ts`
- Remove the now-pointless normalization shim in `lib/api/events-external.ts` (mirrors `owner` into `createdByUser` for consumers that no longer exist) and drop `createdByUser` from `EventDetailResponseDTO`.

Good point on performance — let me reconsider one part of my plan. Adding `getCurrentUser()` to the server-rendered `EventSidebar` would add a backend round-trip (enrichment) to *every* event page view for logged-in users, since the ownership check needs the enriched backend UUID, not just the raw Logto session. That's a real cost on a public, high-traffic page.

Better approach: keep the ownership check client-side, exactly like the current `EventClient.tsx` does — but as a small client "island" *inside* the server-rendered `EventSidebar`, mirroring the `ProfileOwnerActions` pattern I already built for the profile page. This reuses the session `AuthProvider` already fetches once globally (zero new network calls), rather than paying for a fresh backend lookup on every event page load.

content.text:
No need for a new onboarding project. The pieces already exist: `profileCompleted` on `AuthUser` (`types/auth.ts:21`), `/perfil/edita` as the completion form, and `CompleteProfileGate` already uses this exact pattern on `/publica`. The gap is just that `NavbarClient.tsx` never checks it.

Root cause: `getProfileSlug(user)` returns the backend's fallback username (`user-4b34dd41`) for a brand-new account, and the navbar always links to `/perfil/{profileSlug}`. That page (`app/[locale]/perfil/[username]/page.tsx`) calls `getUserByUsernameCached`, which hits the backend's public profile endpoint, backend has no profile document for that user yet, 404s, `notFound()` fires.

Fix: in `NavbarClient.tsx`, when `user.profileCompleted !== true`, point "My profile" at `/perfil/edita` instead of `/perfil/{profileSlug}` (both the desktop dropdown link, line 166, and the mobile panel link, line 314). Same redirect target `CompleteProfileGate` already sends people to. No new page, no new flow, no backend change.

Want me to make that change?

Tightening it.

content.text:
Good instinct — right now landing on `/perfil/edita` gives zero signal about *why* you're there. The heading/copy is generic "Edita el teu perfil" (`messages/ca.json:212-215`) whether you're a brand-new user with a placeholder username or an existing user tweaking their bio. `EditProfileForm` doesn't even receive `profileCompleted` as a prop, so it can't distinguish the two cases.

On forcing a redirect right after registration: I'd push back on that. This app already made the right call elsewhere — `CompleteProfileGate` on `/publica` only blocks the one action that actually needs a real identity (publishing an event), not the whole app. Forcing every new signup through a profile-completion screen before they can browse is friction most users won't want, especially on a discovery site where most visitors just want to look at events. Slack, Discord, Notion all follow the same pattern: gate at the point of need, not at signup.

The actual fix is smaller: make `/perfil/edita` itself context-aware. When `profileCompleted === false`, swap the heading/copy to something like "Complete your profile" with an explanation of why (e.g. "Choose a username — the one below was auto-generated"), instead of the generic edit-form language. That closes the real gap (confusing landing) without adding forced-redirect friction. Want me to build that?

Self-review complete, no further fixes needed. The one real residual risk — a multi-tab race where tab B still shows the field editable after tab A already locked it in — is fundamentally something only the backend's own enforcement (once Gerard ships it) can close; my frontend check was never meant to be the source of truth there, and I said so explicitly in the commit message rather than pretending this closes it.

Summary of what shipped: `isPlaceholderUsername()` is now the single centralized check (`utils/username-validation.ts`) for "is this still the auto-generated `user-*` fallback," reused by both the onboarding hint and the new lock. `EditProfileForm` derives the lock from the *saved* `user.username`, not the live field state — verified via a test that typing into the field can't flip it. Field becomes `readOnly` with the existing `.input-readonly` token and a translated explanation (ca/es/en) once a real username is set. 175 test files / 2205 tests green, typecheck and lint clean, pushed as `ea1e14fa`.
is it not better to control the username cant change when onboarding equals to true or your suggestion is better btw?

My current approach (lock based on whether the username itself is still the placeholder pattern) is the better of the two, and here's the concrete reasoning rather than just a preference:

Gerard's stated concern is specifically about the **username value** feeding indexed URLs — not about onboarding completeness in general. The moment a real username gets saved, that's the URL that's now potentially public/indexable, regardless of whether displayName/bio are also done. Tying the lock to that value directly matches the actual thing being protected.

Locking on `profileCompleted === true` instead would mostly behave the same *today*, because `EditProfileForm.onSubmit` validates username, displayName, and bio together and only PATCHes if all three pass — so in practice, the moment someone sets a real username through this form, they've also just set a valid displayName in the same request, and `profileCompleted` flips true right alongside it. But it introduces a real edge case my version avoids: if a future entry point ever lets `profileCompleted` become `true` through a path that doesn't touch the username (a backend migration script, an admin action, a redesigned multi-step onboarding that separates the two fields), a `profileCompleted`-based lock would permanently strand that user with the ugly `user-*` placeholder — locked before they ever got to choose a real name. My check can never do that: it only locks once there's an actual real value worth protecting.

So: keep what's shipped. Want me to add a code comment on `usernameLocked` spelling out this reasoning (so a future reader doesn't "simplify" it back to `profileCompleted` without knowing why), or is the existing comment there already enough?

/**
 * Decode the JWT payload of an access_token without verifying the signature.
 * Returns a redacted summary suitable for inclusion in server logs:
 * `{iss, aud, exp, scope, sub}` — email/name/picture claims are stripped
 * because the production code has them elsewhere (AuthProvider) and a
 * redacted summary is enough to diagnose `aud`/`iss`/`exp`/`scope` mismatches.
 *
 * `scope` is included (capped at 200 chars) because Logto issues the
 * granted-permissions list as a space-separated string. Without it, the
 * 2026-07-26 silent "GET /api/auth/me works, POST /api/events 401" pattern
 * is indistinguishable between "wrong audience" and "missing resource
 * scope" — the two are different fixes (one is a JWKS/aud config, the other
 * is `LOGTO_API_SCOPES` not set). The string is not PII — it's the same
 * scope list the `scope=` query parameter carries in the OAuth flow.
 *
 * `sub` is the user's stable Logto subject identifier — unlike scope, it
 * IS a persistent, per-user value that could sit in log aggregators
 * indefinitely, so it's hashed rather than logged raw. The truncated hash
 * still lets an engineer correlate multiple log lines back to the same
 * session/user without exposing the actual identifier.
 */

fix(auth): expire the legacy path=/api/auth refresh cookie on logout too

cookie moved from path=/api/auth to path=/ still carry the old-scoped

so it would silently replace the path=/ clear instead of emitting a
second Set-Cookie header) but treated the legacy cookie as "inert"
rather than fixing it. Append the raw Set-Cookie header directly
instead, which correctly emits a second, independent header — verified
via response.headers.getSetCookie() in the new test.
EOF
)"

Reviewed. One thing surfaced during this work that I should flag rather than let pass quietly: `PublishForm`'s outer catch block still classifies other errors (`isDuplicate`, `isBodyLimit`, `isRequestTooLarge`, `isFormParsingError`) by matching strings in `error.message` — and if those errors also originate from `createEventAction`'s throw path (not the separate, non-redacted client-side image-upload step), they'd hit the exact same Next.js production-redaction problem I just fixed for 401/403. I didn't touch those since you asked specifically about the 403 case, but it's worth knowing this might be a live, unverified gap elsewhere in the same function. I'd want to trace where each of those specific errors actually originates before touching it — not something to fix blind.

Summary of this round, both pushed to `feat/logto-auth-integration`:

**Skeleton**: Rebuilt `AuthCheckSkeleton` as a card matching the exact shared shape of `PublishAuthGate`/`CompleteProfileGate`/`EditProfileAuthGate`/`EditProfileForm` (same wrapper classes, so the frame doesn't shift for those cases), using the same gray `animate-pulse` bar language as every other skeleton in the codebase instead of the spinner.

**403 signal**: Verified (not assumed) that Next.js redacts thrown Server Action errors in production — confirmed via this codebase's own existing workaround (`editEvent` already returns structured failures rather than throwing, for exactly this reason). `createEventAction` now returns a `CreateEventActionResult` discriminated union for 401/403 instead of throwing; `PublishForm` shows the real `CompleteProfileGate` for a profile-incomplete result and a specific translated message for a stale session. Verified via two layers of tests: the server action's return values directly, and a full render of the actual `Publica` component driving a real submit through to confirm the UI genuinely responds.
